title: Policy Wording Comparison Assistant
summary: Align two or more policy wordings clause by clause, highlight what was added, removed, narrowed or broadened, and answer questions with citations to the exact clause.

seo.title: Policy Wording Comparison with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that compares insurance policy wordings clause by clause, flags material changes in cover, exclusions and limits, and cites the source clause.

designed_for: Product Manager, Health or Commercial Lines

problem.intro: Policy wordings change at every renewal, product refile and negotiation with a corporate client's broker. A narrowed definition, a new sub-limit or a moved exclusion can hide inside a document that looks almost identical to last year's, and finding it means slow, careful reading line by line.

pain_points.title: Renumbered clauses defeat redlines
pain_points.detail: Word-processor comparisons break when sections are reordered or renumbered, producing pages of noise and hiding the real changes.

pain_points.title: Meaning changes, not just words
pain_points.detail: Replacing 'any' with 'the' or adding one qualifying phrase to a definition can change cover materially without looking like a big edit.

pain_points.title: Comparisons across insurers are inconsistent
pain_points.detail: Brokers building group health or property comparisons extract room-rent limits, co-pays, deductibles and exclusions by hand, and each insurer's format differs.

pain_points.title: Customer summaries drift from the wording
pain_points.detail: Brochures and customer information sheets can fall out of step with the filed wording after several revisions.

solution.overview: We build a comparison assistant that reads policy wordings, endorsements and customer-facing summaries and breaks each into clauses with their numbering and headings. It aligns equivalent clauses across documents even when they are reordered or renamed, then classifies each difference as added, removed, narrowed, broadened or editorial. A parameter table pulls the items your team cares about, such as waiting periods, sub-limits, co-pay, deductibles and territorial limits, into one view with clause citations. Users can ask questions across the documents and get answers that quote the clause or say it was not found. It is a drafting and review aid, not a coverage opinion.
capabilities: Segments wordings, endorsements and schedules into clauses, keeping numbering and headings
Aligns equivalent clauses across versions and insurers, even when reordered or renamed
Classifies each difference as added, removed, narrowed, broadened or editorial
Builds a parameter table for limits, waiting periods, co-pays, deductibles and exclusions, with citations
Checks customer information sheets and brochures against the wording for inconsistencies
Answers questions across the document set, quoting the clause or stating that it was not found

workflow.title: Load the document set
workflow.detail: Users upload the wordings, endorsements and summaries to compare, tagged by version and source.

workflow.title: Segment into clauses
workflow.detail: Each document is split into clauses with numbering, headings and cross-references preserved.

workflow.title: Align equivalent clauses
workflow.detail: Clauses are matched across documents, and low-confidence alignments are flagged for a reviewer.

workflow.title: Classify differences
workflow.detail: Each aligned pair is labelled by type of change, with the changed text highlighted.

workflow.title: Build the comparison table
workflow.detail: Agreed parameters are extracted into a table, with each cell citing its clause.

workflow.title: Review and export
workflow.detail: A product, legal or placement reviewer confirms material differences and exports the redline and table.

inputs: Policy wordings, current and proposed or expiring
Customer information sheet, prospectus or brochure
Schedule of benefits or policy schedule
Broker manuscript wording or client requirement list
outputs: Difference register with change type and citations
Parameter comparison table in Excel or PDF
Consistency flags between customer summaries and the wording
human_in_the_loop: Product, legal or placement staff review every difference marked as material before it is used in a filing, a client comparison or a negotiation. The assistant never states whether a specific loss or claim is covered.
guardrails: Answers only from the uploaded documents, with clause citations
States 'not found' instead of filling gaps from general knowledge
Material-change labels confirmed by a person before export
Exact document versions recorded for every comparison
No coverage opinions or claim decisions
compliance_notes: Helps product and compliance teams check that customer information sheets and brochures match the wording, in line with IRDAI's emphasis on clear and consistent disclosure to policyholders.
Outputs are review aids for qualified staff, not legal advice.

pilot.scope: One product family, such as retail health indemnity, comparing the current wording with its previous version, its customer information sheet and two public competitor wordings.
deliverables: Parameter list agreed with product and legal teams
Working comparison assistant on the pilot document set
Accuracy report on alignment and difference classification
Roll-out plan for other product lines or broker use

what_we_measure.how: Reviewer checks of matched clause pairs across the pilot documents.
Tool output compared with a reviewer's independent comparison of one document pair.
Share of table cells and answers whose cited clause actually supports the value.
Timed for the pilot comparison against the team's usual manual method.

faqs.q: Can it compare scanned or older wordings?
faqs.a: Yes. Scanned wordings go through OCR first, and the clause segmenter handles older numbering styles. Pages with poor scan quality are flagged so a reviewer can check the text.

faqs.q: Can it tell us whether a claim would be covered?
faqs.a: No. It shows what the wordings say and where they differ, with citations. Coverage decisions belong to your claims and legal teams.

faqs.q: Does it work for group health and commercial wordings as well as retail products?
faqs.a: Yes. The parameter list is configurable, so a broker comparing group health terms and an underwriter reviewing a property endorsement can each use their own set of fields.

faqs.q: Is our unpublished product wording safe?
faqs.a: Documents stay in your environment or a dedicated cloud tenancy, access is role-based, and model endpoints are configured not to retain or train on your content.
